entities.name: Query protein 768 aa
observations: Sequence length is 768 aa; estimated molecular mass is 85.0 kDa and theoretical pI is 6.41.
Pfam matches support an N-terminal aminoadipic-semialdehyde-synthase/lysine-ketoglutarate-reductase module and a C-terminal saccharopine-dehydrogenase module.
Best reviewed homologs are mammalian mitochondrial alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthases with 52.9–53.9% identity and 97.5–99.7% query coverage.

Most likely function is bifunctional catalysis of the first two steps of lysine degradation through the saccharopine pathway; exact substrate/cofactor specificity remains homology-supported rather than experimentally established for this sequence.

Likely mitochondrial, probably matrix-localized, based on close homolog annotations; this sequence begins with a basic, Arg-rich region consistent with a possible mitochondrial targeting peptide, but localization is not experimentally established here.
Likely biological processes include L-lysine catabolism and generation of precursor metabolites/energy.
Sequence-derived properties: gravy -0.2415, charge at pH 7 approximately -6.06, instability index 43.2; these are computational estimates.

entities.name: Alpha-aminoadipic semialdehyde synthase
observations: Reviewed mammalian homologs A8E657, A2VCW9, and Q99K67 are annotated as bifunctional enzymes catalyzing the first two steps of lysine degradation.
Annotated EC activities include lysine-ketoglutarate reductase activity (EC 1.5.1.8) and saccharopine dehydrogenase activity (EC 1.5.1.9).
Reviewed homologs are localized to mitochondria or mitochondrial matrix and form homotetramers.

entities.name: L-lysine degradation
observations: The saccharopine pathway degrades L-lysine through a mitochondrial bifunctional enzyme catalyzing its first two steps.
The pathway contributes to amino-acid degradation and can support generation of precursor metabolites and energy.

entities.name: Saccharopine pathway first two steps
observations: Candidate reaction evidence includes L-saccharopine + NADP(+) + H2O = L-lysine + 2-oxoglutarate + NADPH + H(+), mapped to Rhea RHEA:19373.
A second mapped reaction is L-saccharopine + NAD(+) + H2O = (S)-2-amino-6-oxohexanoate + L-glutamate + NADH + H(+), mapped to Rhea RHEA:24520.
The tool reports multiple reaction candidates; exact direction and cofactor usage should not be assigned with certainty from homology alone.
